analysis.title: S&P Global Inc. (SPGI): 3Q beat-and-raise, with the strategic review of CapIQ creating a potential source of value creation
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on SPGI and raises the 12-month price target from $519 to $532 (23.5x unchanged on rolled-forward NTM+1YR EPS of $22.64), 18.5% upside from $448.93.
3Q26 revenue was $3,678mn, +6.8% y/y (7.1% OCC), versus GS estimate of 5.6% growth and FactSet consensus of 5.8%. Energy, Indices and Market Intelligence beat, Ratings was a modest miss.
3Q26 adjusted EPS was $4.58 versus GS estimate $4.39 and consensus $4.43. Operating margin rose 60 bps y/y to 53.5%, versus GS 51.6% and consensus 52.6%.

SPGI is evaluating a separation of CapIQ and associated data businesses (Financials, SNL, Visible Alpha), the majority of Kensho Data & Platforms. It would retain Enterprise Solutions, RatingsDirect and RatingsXpress. Advisers are engaged, NDAs signed with several interested parties, and clarity is expected by February.
Kensho Data & Platforms grew 6% organically in 3Q, with double-digit growth in Kensho Data, versus 8% organic growth (7% subscription) in retained Enterprise Solutions.

Hyperscaler debt issuance reached ~$240bn YTD against SPGI's full-year outlook of $250-300bn. SPGI raised its 2026 M&A issuance outlook to 20-30% growth. The ~$11tn refinancing pipeline through 2030 and nearly $3tn of 2027 remaining performance obligations across four hyperscalers support issuance.

SPGI expects 4Q26 Ratings transaction revenue to decline slightly y/y on difficult comparisons and an investment-grade-weighted mix. Higher rates are a headwind for high yield and leveraged loans. Ratings margins contracted ~130 bps y/y in 3Q.
The CBOE extension runs through 2051, pulls forward the improved economics by six years, and should add a couple percentage points to Indices revenue growth in 2027.

SPGI named Kalshi its preferred but nonexclusive prediction-market partner, with two opportunities: licensing indices for contract resolution and building new indices from prediction-market data. No products or launch dates are disclosed.

AI monetization is broadening. Discrete AI products added ~50 bps to 3Q growth in both Energy and Kensho Data & Platforms. AI customers' ACV growth was 1.8x non-AI customers in Market Intelligence and ~3x in Energy. API calls rose nearly 50% q/q and >4,000% y/y.

SPGI expects to repurchase more than $7bn of shares in 2026, double the original $3.5bn plan, after $4bn through 3Q and a new $2.6bn launched in the quarter. It plans ~$2bn of new debt to help fund it.

Energy grew 6% organically in 3Q including a ~50 bps sanctions headwind. Demand is constrained across LNG, refined products and chemicals, and strong one-time 3Q sales may not recur in 4Q. The upstream software divestiture and Data Center Hawk acquisition will pressure 4Q reported growth and margins.
2026 guidance was raised: OCC revenue growth to 7.5-8.5% (from 6.0-8.0%), operating margin expansion to 75-100 bps (from 35-60 bps), EPS to $17.70-17.95 (from $17.50-17.75).

GS raises 2026/27/28 revenue estimates by an average of 1.1% on Energy and Indices strength, and operating margin estimates on Ratings. EPS moves to $17.82/$20.39/$23.36 from $17.77/$20.53/$23.64 on higher interest expense.
Guidance points to negative consensus revisions for revenue, positive revisions for operating margin and largely stable consensus EPS.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised from $519 to $532 after a 3Q beat and guidance raise. GS cites debt issuance, index benchmark adoption, AI monetization and the CapIQ strategic review as drivers.

sector_views.rationale: GS applies a 23.5x target multiple to SPGI, above the Info Services peer median of 15.8x, citing execution, a proprietary data moat and higher EBITDA margins.

earnings_insights: SPGI 3Q26 (reported 10/27/26): revenue $3,678mn reported, +6.8% y/y, versus GS estimate $3,636mn and GS-cited growth estimate 5.6% and FactSet consensus growth 5.8%.
SPGI 3Q26 adjusted EPS $4.58 reported versus GS estimate $4.39 and FactSet consensus $4.43. GAAP EPS $4.45 reported versus GS estimate $4.13.
3Q26 segment revenue y/y reported: Ratings +2.5% (GS est. 3.3%), Market Intelligence +6.8% (GS est. 4.6%), Energy +5.9% (GS est. 3.0%), Indices +19.9% (GS est. 17.0%).
3Q26 adjusted operating margin 53.5% reported versus GS estimate 51.6% and consensus 52.6%.
4Q26E GS adjusted EPS cut to $3.94 from $4.08, with revenue raised to $3,613mn from $3,564mn. FY26E EPS $17.82 (prior $17.77), FY27E $20.39 (prior $20.53), FY28E $23.36 (prior $23.64).
Pre-print GS FY26 estimates were revenue growth 7.4%, operating margin 52.0%, EPS $17.77. FactSet consensus was revenue growth 9.1%, operating margin 51.4%, EPS $17.84.

Company FY26 guidance after the print: OCC revenue growth 7.5-8.5%, reported revenue growth 7.4-8.4%, EPS $17.70-17.95. Segment OCC growth guidance: Ratings 6.5-8.0%, Market Intelligence 5.5-7.0%, Energy 4.5-6.0%, Indices 17.0-18.5%.
Share repurchases expected above $7bn in 2026, versus the original $3.5bn plan.

trade_ideas.rationale: Organic growth and margin expansion, durable debt financing activity, index benchmark adoption, AI monetization, higher buybacks and the CapIQ strategic review.
trade_ideas.risk: Moderation in debt issuance growth, financial services budget and headcount pressures on Market Intelligence, a market pull-back weighing on Indices, and FX.

risk_factors: Moderation in debt issuance volume growth.
Financial services budget and headcount pressures that could weigh on Market Intelligence growth.
A market pull-back that could put downward pressure on Indices growth.
The CapIQ perimeter, stranded costs and financial profiles of the resulting companies are not yet defined.
Unresolved allocation of Kensho teams and capabilities creates uncertainty around SPGI's retained AI strategy.
Higher interest rates are a headwind for high yield and leveraged loans, and an investment-grade-heavy mix pressures Ratings transaction revenue in 4Q.
geopolitical: Energy visibility is limited in the near term given geopolitical volatility, and sanctions were a ~50 bps headwind to 3Q Energy organic growth.

tension_points.bull_case: A separation of CapIQ and associated data businesses could increase investment focus and leave a portfolio centered on SPGI's credit, equities and commodities franchises. GS sees it as another potential source of value creation.
tension_points.bear_case: The perimeter is not finalized, revenue and margin profiles are not disclosed, and stranded costs, commercial arrangements and the allocation of Kensho's AI teams are unresolved.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Greater clarity expected by February on the separation outcome and perimeter.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler financing, improving M&A issuance and the ~$11tn refinancing pipeline through 2030 support debt issuance.
tension_points.bear_case: SPGI expects 4Q transaction revenue to decline slightly y/y on difficult comps, higher rates and an investment-grade-heavy mix.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Moderation in debt issuance volume growth would undermine the bull case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Continued hyperscaler financing, improving M&A activity and the refinancing pipeline support debt issuance despite a 4Q Ratings transaction headwind.
